conviction_note: abs_move 9.0 (option-implied 9.24, median |6.5|, last four prints 32/0.9/15/-6.5) times a p_up of 55: the findings genuinely offset (US agency hours and the company's own Q4 hiring survey are up, European peer updates and BLS and a Q4 FX headwind are down) and sum to 0.0, while the scaled number leans slightly positive on positioning (9.8% of float short, stock -11.5% in 20 days into a bar the company set itself with stable July exit trends); the gap between 0.0 and +0.9 is that lean and nothing else.
bar: EPS: company guide $0.96-1.06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000871763/000119312526305399/man-ex99_1.htm, 2026-07-16); consensus $1.01 (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/MAN/earnings-forecasts) and $1.03 (a second aggregator, via search) - two sources that disagree by 2c, so the EPS bar is the guide midpoint ~$1.01. Revenue: Benzinga $4.86B, but the call guided organic days-adjusted cc growth 3-7% (midpoint 5%, ~6% after days/dispositions) on a Q3 2025 base near $4.5B with EUR roughly -1% YoY, which implies ~$4.75-4.80B reported, so the revenue bar is unverified and every size here is capped small. print_vs_bar is on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,426,985 shares, 9.81% of float, 5.38 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down from 10.8% (8/14) and 10.0% (9/15) - MarketBeat/FINRA, page updated 2026-10-09 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MAN/short-interest). Sweep row carries the same 4.4M / 5.4 DTC from curvedtrading. Skew is null in the baseline (no 25d skew computed); put/call OI 0.98, total OI 2,695, ATM IV 128.9%, implied event move 9.24%. The stock is -11.5% over 20 days and -18.55% off its 52w high, after Hays (-9% on 10-12), Michael Page (slipped on 10-13) and the BLS temp-help print (10-02). A moderately crowded short into a derated name: a beat has a squeeze mechanism; a miss has sellers already in place.

findings.finding: US agency-reported staffing demand accelerated through the end of Q3: SIA|Bullhorn US staffing hours were +9% year-over-year in the week ended 2026-09-26 (a new year-to-date high, industrial +15%, IT +6%, office/clerical -8%), and the ASA Staffing Index was +3.3% YoY for the week of Sept 7-13; Manpower US grew 16% in Q2 and management guided US Q3 growth 'similar to Q2', so the US line (Q2 revenue $714m, operating profit $52.8m, the largest profit swing in the group) is tracking at or above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-16: a Q2 beat led by US Manpower +16% and Experis improvement was bought +32.37% (baseline). 2025-10-16: a Q3 beat was sold -6.52% on the Q4 guide. The US line has paid when it surprised up.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 11.5% in the 20 days into the print, the period in which these weekly readings were published, so the price is carrying the BLS and European-peer negatives, not these; if the market had priced +9% US hours the stock would not be -18.5% off its July high with 9.8% of float short. US is ~15% of revenue but ~30% of segment operating profit, so it is sized net of the European majority.
findings.independence: ASA Staffing Index +3.3% YoY, week Sept 7-13 (https://americanstaffing.net/research/asa-staffing-industry-data/staffing-index/). Michael Page US gross profit +7% in Q3 2026, eighth consecutive quarter of growth, construction +12% (https://investors.michaelpage.com/~/media/Files/P/page-v2/ir/result-reports/2026/q3-2026-trading-statement.pdf, 2026-10-13). SThree US net fees +11% in the quarter to 31 Aug (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sthree--stem/fy26-q3-trading-update/9783226). Proxies, not company numbers; the BLS series in the next finding contradicts them.

findings.finding: BLS temporary help services employment fell 10,900 in September 2026 (released 2026-10-02), the largest monthly decline of the year, with July revised from +5,200 to -10,000 and August from +6,800 to +200, so the broad government series has Q3 US temp employment down on net while the agency indices above have hours up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior MAN print in the baseline turned on BLS data; the series is a macro proxy for the US Manpower line, which bought +32% in July 2026 on company numbers that contradicted a soft BLS tape.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the stock fell 3.0% over the five sessions around and after the release and 11.5% over twenty. Filed because it is the broadest public US series and contradicts the agency readings; a market that had fully priced it would not also carry the agency-reported acceleration unpriced. Sized small because the company's own Q2 US number (+16%) diverged from BLS in the same direction last quarter.
findings.independence: BLS Employment Situation, September 2026, total nonfarm +29,000, unemployment 4.2%, July/August revised down a combined 60,000 (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Same line as the finding above, opposite sign: the two are filed apart so a judge can weigh them.

findings.finding: Three European recruiters have reported the September quarter since ManpowerGroup last spoke and the temp side of Europe is flat to slightly up while France and Germany are weak: Michael Page (2026-10-13) EMEA gross profit -3.8% cc with temporary +2% and permanent -7%, France -11% (temp -8%, perm -15%), Germany -7% (contracting +15%), Southern Europe +5% (Spain +9%), UK -5.5% (temp +2%); Hays (2026-10-12) group net fees -3% LFL, temp & contracting -1%, France -16% with temp growing, Germany hours stable; SThree (2026-09-22) contract fees -1%. ManpowerGroup guided France 'flat to slight growth' and Italy 'low-to-mid single digit' for Q3; France is $1.18bn of $4.86bn quarterly revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-04-17: -19.07% on a France/Europe-led miss and weak guide. 2026-04-16: +0.88% on an in-line quarter. France has been the line that hurt this name most when it surprised down.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Hays fell ~9% and MAN fell with the sector this week. What is not in the price is the split - the peers' temp/contracting lines in Europe are flat to positive (Page temp +2%, Hays T&C -1%) and Southern Europe is growing, while their perm lines carry the declines; ManpowerGroup is ~85% temp/staffing. Sized net of Italy/Spain growth; the French temp readings from perm-heavy peers are a weak proxy for Manpower France's industrial temp book.
findings.independence: Hays Q1 FY27 trading statement, 2026-10-12 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/hays--has/first-quarter-trading-statement/9816766; figures via https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/hays-q1-net-fee-decline-narrows-to-3-but-permanent-hiring-falls). SThree Q3 FY26, 2026-09-22 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sthree--stem/fy26-q3-trading-update/9783226). INSEE flash: French interim employment -1.4% q/q in Q2 2026, -1.9% YoY (https://www.insee.fr/fr/statistiques/fichier/version-html/9032830/IR186_FlashEmp_2T2026.pdf), against Prism'emploi May 2026 +0.5% YoY, the first annual rise since Dec 2022 (https://www.prismemploi.eu/sites/default/files/2026-07/Barometre_Prismemploi_mai_2026_BOURGOGNE-FRANCHE-COMTE.pdf). All proxies.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide will carry a larger currency headwind than Q3's: EUR/USD is 1.1195 at the ECB fix on 2026-10-14 against a Q4 2025 average of about 1.160 (-3.5% YoY), whereas Q3 2026 averaged about 1.151 against Q3 2025's 1.161 (-0.9%), consistent with the 2c unfavourable impact the Q3 guide assumed; with roughly two-thirds of revenue in euro-area currencies, a Q4 guide struck at spot embeds a ~2 point reported-revenue headwind and roughly 4-5c of EPS against the prior-year quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-16: -6.52% when a Q3 beat came with a Q4 guide the market read as disappointing. 2026-01-29: +14.95% on a Q1 guide read as a turn. This name trades on the guide more than on the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: FX is visible to everyone, so most of it is priced; what is not is the mechanical translation into the headline Q4 EPS range on a day the market reads the range before the constant-currency detail. If priced, the stock would already sit at a Q4 EPS consensus marked to 1.12, which the two aggregator estimates (built in July-August at 1.14-1.16) are not. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 monthly averages computed from daily ECB-based mid rates (July 1.1608, Aug 1.1604, Sep 1.1613, Oct 1.1604, Nov 1.1596, Dec 1.1611) at https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/EUR-USD-2025. The 2c Q3 FX assumption and 44% tax rate are in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000871763/000119312526305399/man-ex99_1.htm). Arithmetic is mine; the FX move is a fact.

findings.finding: ManpowerGroup's own Q4 2026 Employment Outlook Survey (2026-09-08) has the global Net Employment Outlook at 29%, +2 points on Q3 and +6 points year-over-year, with the US at 36%, UK 23%, Germany 15% and France 13%, and 43% of employers planning to add staff in Q4 against 14% cutting - the company's own forward demand gauge improved into the quarter it is about to guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The MEOS is released a month before each print and has not itself moved the stock; the Q4 guide has (2025-10-16 -6.52%, 2026-01-29 +14.95%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a survey of hiring intentions, not revenue, and the stock has fallen 11.5% since it was published, so the market has given it no weight; if it had, a +6 point YoY improvement in the company's own gauge would not coexist with a derating into the print. Sized small because the survey has a loose link to billed hours.
findings.independence: Korn Ferry fiscal Q1 (to 2026-07-31, released 2026-09-09): fee revenue +7%, growth in every region, remaining contracted fees +14% (https://ir.kornferry.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000056679-26-000029/kfy-20260731xex991q1fy27.htm). Deutsche Bank's 2026-09-09 sector note estimates ~50% of peer recruitment revenue back in growth vs ~10% in Q1 2025 (https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1098288/deutsche-bank-upgrades-robert-walters-and-lifts-target-to-160p-1098288.html). Same company as the next finding, different survey.

findings.finding: The company's US tech hiring outlook for Q4 2026 (Experis US, released 2026-09-22) is 37%, down 10 points from both the prior quarter and the prior year, with the Experis US president saying tech hiring is 'moderating'; Experis US was flat in Q2 (-3% ex healthcare IT projects) and management guided it to 'slight growth' in Q3, so the company's own forward gauge for that line weakened after the guide was set.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Experis improvement was one of the named drivers of the +32% July 2026 reaction; a reversal on that line has not been tested in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: A sub-survey of the company's own MEOS that no aggregator carries against the Experis line; if the market had read it, previews would flag Experis US risk, and the Q2 narrative of Experis 'turning' is what the wire still carries. Experis global is ~20% of revenue and the US slice is a fraction, so it is sized small and net of Manpower US strength.
findings.independence: SIA|Bullhorn IT staffing hours +6% YoY in the week to 2026-09-26, below industrial +15% (https://www.staffingindustry.com/research/research-reports/americas/sia-bullhorn-staffing-indicator-october-6-2026), the only independent series and it points mildly the other way. Shares the MEOS instrument with the previous finding; opposite sign on a different segment.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is one-sided short on a company-set bar: 9.81% of float short, 5.38 days to cover (2026-09-30 settlement), the stock -11.5% over 20 sessions and -18.55% off the July high, while the company's own guide ($0.96-1.06) was set with France 'stable throughout' Q2, US 'strengthening through the quarter' and Italy 'exiting solid', and consensus ($1.01-1.03) sits at the guide midpoint - the short is positioned for a guide the company has not signalled it will miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-16: +32.37% with 10.7% of float short (MarketBeat 7/31 row) on a beat at a low bar; 2025-04-17: -19.07% when a crowded name missed. The squeeze has run in both directions on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price; what is filed is the asymmetry it creates - a crowded short into an in-line print has to cover, and the free control (-run_up_20d) points the same way. If the derating were company-specific rather than sector-sympathy there would be a MAN-specific note or 8-K behind it, and there is none since 2026-08-11.
findings.independence: Sweep row: 4.4M shares, 9.5% of shares outstanding, 5.4 DTC at the same settlement via curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/man/short-interest/). Q2 call exit-rate commentary (https://www.webull.com/news/15237291763917824, 2026-07-16). The -11.5% run-up is in the sealed baseline.

baseline_tension: The findings net to zero and the scaled lean is mildly positive, which cuts against the -11.5% run-up and the sector sell-off of the last three sessions but agrees with the free control (-run_up) and with a 9.8%-of-float short; skew is null so there is no option-market directional statement to beat.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a proxy that contradicts a broad public series is sized below it): the US agency-series finding (SIA|Bullhorn +9%, ASA +3.3%) was cut from +1.5 to +1.2 because the BLS temp-help series, the broadest public US number, has September -10,900 with July and August revised down; both are filed

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the revenue consensus ($4.86B) could not be reconciled with the company's cc growth guide and is declared unverified in `bar`; the EPS bar is the company guide plus two aggregators 2c apart; sizes were already capped small and were not changed further

Rules 1, 3, 7, 9 checked and left standing: findings already named their line, were sized net of the rest of the company, carried no self-rebutting caveat, and the sign agrees with the short-interest asymmetry; p_up left at 55
Net effect: impact_sum moved from +0.3 to 0.0; abs_move, p_up, expected_move and print_vs_bar unchanged
